title: Android/iOS porting of a RPG MAKER XP game!

posts.author: KayThePianist
posts.body:
Hello guys, I've spent an intense year and developed a complex and ambitious JRPG with RPG MAKER XP, now available on Steam:
I would love so much to port it on Android and maybe iOS.
It's possible or it needs some extra intense coding?
If it needs writing some codes, is there anyone interested in making the porting?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
That question is a bit more compley than you think.
First, you would need an androd player for RMXP-data.
That is made more difficult by the graphics library being closed source and never published.
Someone made such a player by illegal reverse engineering years ago, but for a commercial game an illegal player is a no-go. I only mention this here so you can be careful if you see linkes there.
Howeverthere was also a project to replace the closed-source graphics library in a legal way with a DirectX-compatible one.
Unfortunately I do not know if that project was completed and if they went on to an android version after that. But it is one thing you should search for.
Second, how many scripts are you using in your game?
if your game is script-heavy that will be an additional problem in porting.
Because I heard that Ruby-scripts (which the RMXP is based on) have problems on mobiles (that is one of the reasons they changed the script base to javascript with MV/MZ).

posts.author: kyonides
posts.body: JoiPlay with its RPG Maker extension can help you run most of RMXP games on Android. I posted a phone screenshot of KBribe XP, my custom RGSS script, weeks ago. This extension is based on an open source project called mkxp-z. It uses its own set of technologies so it can run on Windows, Linux and yes, even Android.

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
Yes, To The Moon was completely re-created with Unity.
This has been the case for a few RPG Maker games that were ported to either different versions of RPG Maker (a lot of the old horror games got ported over to MV) or different engines entirely (Ara Fell was ported to Unity as well).
Worst case, you could always sell your game on Steam/Itch.io and tell players they might be able to play it on their smartphone with an emulator. The heavier your game is on scripting, though, the less likely it is to be compatible with such things.

posts.author: kyonides
posts.body:
Stop lying, Prescott. To the Moon is STILL a RMXP game. Plus, Ara Fell was originally made with RM2K3 not XP, but yes, it was later ported to Unity indeed.
Not claiming you're doing it on purpose at all. It's just that I can't stand any inaccurate depictions of stuff people never cared to confirm. Especially if it's related to old RM engines.
EDIT: The following line proves it's linked to the mkxp project, which could also let To the Moon be ported to Linux.
Ruby:
MKXP.puts("[#{@dll}:#{@func}] #{args.inspect}") if !@called
This piece of code was found on a preload script. Why did the project need it as a separate script? I dunno. Anyway, that's one of mkxp's original features.

posts.author: kyonides
posts.body:
Even the Windows release of that game uses mkxp. It's interesting to hear it has been ported to mobile platforms as well.
Actually, some time after Ancurio finished the Linux port of mkxp, he managed to release a windows binary compiled against Ruby 2.1. AFAIK, it's the last link of the original binaries that's still available online. I think it was compiled back in 2015 or 2018. There were Linux executables on his web hosting site, but he let that account expired about a year ago.
Even so it makes me think you are confused with the release dates of the Windows / Linux games and the mobile ones. I'll try to check that out but it's not a priority right now.
